title: Jad workspace.json (workspace layout)
description: W/.jad/workspace.json turns the workspace layout on for a server started in W (docs/design_workspace_layout.md): W keeps its sessions (W/.jad/sessions), profiles (W/.jad/profiles), private models and tools (W/.jad/models, W/.jad/tools) and state (W/.jad/state); the shared catalogs come from the global folder (global.schema.json). A W/.jad/setting.json is then not read. Read once at start. Deleting this file goes back to the setting.json layout. An unknown key is refused; for the start workspace that refuses the start, for a listed one it skips the workspace.

remote_keys.description: Names of the key files (G/auth/keys/<key>.json, kind remote_key, mode 0600) whose credentials the workspace may use for the remote bindings (G/remotes/<binding>.json) the key files name. Every profile of this workspace unless its session or the profile sets its own list. Absent inherits from the level above, [] means no keys, a non-empty list replaces the levels above. A key only supplies the bearer token of its binding and never widens what a tool may reach: that is the remotes list of each tool. A broken key (missing file, wrong permissions, a binding that does not exist, two keys for one binding) fails the runs that use it, naming the key. Workspace layout only; never a key of a toolset.

id.description: The workspace id when global.json does not list this workspace (default: the folder name made an id). When it is listed, the id must be the listed one.

defaults.description: Setting values every session of this workspace starts from, over global.json defaults. A relative env_file is relative to W/.jad, a relative cwd to W; without any cwd a session works in W. A profile may tighten, never loosen, the caps and an enabled sandbox set here or in global.json.

libraries.description: The workspace's own content library and tool definition files, seen only by this workspace: folders relative to this file's folder (W/.jad), read once at start, listed after the global ones. None by default. A skill or command name also in the global library is left out and naming it is an error; prompts and templates of both are listed side by side.

tool_definition_paths.description: Native tool definition files of this workspace, read after the ones in G/global.json. Entries are non-empty literal paths or host-native Go filepath.Glob patterns (*, ?, bracket classes; no recursive **, shell, tilde or environment expansion). Patterns expand once at process startup, in entry order with sorted matches, and cleaned absolute paths are deduplicated keeping the first occurrence. Runtime rejects malformed patterns and patterns with no matches; missing literal paths retain deferred validation. Unescaped metacharacters now mean patterns; platform escaping follows Go filepath semantics. Matched directories and invalid documents are not skipped. A relative path is relative to this file's folder (W/.jad); a path may also be absolute. The same tool ID in two files is an error naming both. A file in the folders a profile writes (W/.jad/profile-own, W/.jad/data, W/.jad/profiles), in G/auth or in another workspace's .jad is refused. Every file is read-only in a sandbox of this workspace.

profile_message.description: The profile_message policy of this workspace (docs/design_workspace_layout.md §30.3). Workspaces listed in G/global.json workspaces trust each other: a profile reaches any profile of any listed workspace by local:<workspace>/<session>/<category>/<name>; the consent of the target (accept_from) no longer exists and is refused by name. deny rules only refuse; allow_reset is the one thing this workspace can allow. This file is read-only in every sandbox and a profile cannot change it.

deny.description: Calls this workspace refuses, one list for both directions: a rule that matches a call whose caller or target is in this workspace refuses it (so {} means this workspace neither sends nor receives profile_message). A rule without from matches any caller, including a remote one; a rule with from matches local callers only. The refusal is profile_denied with by workspace:<id>, never a path or a rule.

allow_reset.description: Resets of this workspace's profiles that a profile of another workspace may cause with a reset context_trigger. Absent or empty: refused (profile_denied, action reset), and the call is not sent without the reset. A deny rule that matches wins. Resets inside this workspace need no rule, and a remote caller cannot reset.

profile_self_edit.description: The profile_self_edit level of this workspace: off, on or full (see global.schema.json). It can only lower the level of G/global.json (on when unset): a workspace that sets full while global.json does not stays on.

localPattern.description: A glob over a canonical local address local:<workspace>/<session>/<category>/<name>: '*' and '?' never cross a '/', there are no classes and no short forms.

anyPattern.description: A glob over a canonical address, local:<workspace>/<session>/<category>/<name> or remote:<binding>/<session>/<category>/<name>.

from.description: The calling profile (a local address); any caller when absent.

to.description: The target profile; any target when absent.

actions.description: What the rule refuses. message (the default) refuses the whole call and so implies the others; reset and compact refuse a call whose caller's context_trigger has that action (judged before anything is queued); model_choice refuses a call that names a model.

from.description: The calling profile (a local address); any caller when absent.

to.description: The target profile; its workspace must be this workspace's own id. Any profile of this workspace when absent.
